title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Ethiopia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Ethiopia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Ethiopia: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: Coordinating medical records, legal representation, social security benefits, and cross-border authentication during a serious illness in Ethiopia requires navigating a mixed digital and in-person administrative landscape. While several federal websites operate live (such as eservices.gov.et, justice.gov.et, moh.gov.et, psssa.gov.et, and poessa.gov.et), other Ethiopian government portals experience intermittent outages, incomplete subpages, or TLS certificate errors from abroad (for example, mfa.gov.et fails standard certificate checks), and consular offices have shifted toward online Digital MoFA workflows. Consequently, this guide pairs live federal agency and Ethiopian diplomatic mission pages with verified international legal archives (FAOLEX, ILO NATLEX, Refworld, and HCCH) and foreign consular notices, and you should confirm current office procedures directly with the relevant federal bureau or embassy.

steps.title: Secure medical records and coordinate palliative and hospital care
steps.html:
• Request complete signed copies of hospital medical summaries, imaging, laboratory results, and clinical capacity assessments from the treating institution in Ethiopia, guided nationally by the Ministry of Health Palliative Care Strategic Document [1].
  • Document care preferences and authorize trusted family members directly with attending physicians, because Ethiopian federal statutes do not establish a public electronic living-will or advance-directive registry and medical decision-making relies on clinical consent and family or appointed legal representatives.

steps.title: Execute and authenticate a Power of Attorney (Wekilina)
steps.html:
• Authorize a trusted representative in Ethiopia to handle banking, property, court, or benefit filings by executing a formal Power of Attorney (wekilina) before the Documents Authentication and Registration Service (DARS) under Proclamation No. 922/2015 on Authentication and Registration of Documents and Council of Ministers Regulation No. 451/2019 (fees), published by the Ministry of Justice of Ethiopia [3][4].
  • Book domestic authentication or agency appointments through the federal electronic services portal (Ethiopian Government eServices Portal, technical support 888) and regional DARS branches [2].
  • When the patient is outside Ethiopia, apply through accredited Ethiopian consular services such as the Embassy of Ethiopia in Washington, D.C., noting that physical walk-in Power of Attorney and authentication counters transitioned in April 2026 to online submission via Digital MoFA and consular portals (USD 62 fee for holders of valid Ethiopian passports or Ethiopian Origin ID cards, or USD 95 for other nationals, via money order) [8][9][10].

steps.title: Verify civil status records, capacity, and guardianship rules
steps.html:
• Confirm that vital identity records, Ethiopian Origin ID (Yellow Card) files, passports, and municipal civil status registrations match official agency rules before any notarized or court transaction [14].
  • Review marital property, household representation, legal capacity, and judicial interdiction or guardianship rules under Ethiopia's Revised Family Code Proclamation No. 213/2000 (applying in federal jurisdictions alongside regional family codes) and Book One of the Civil Code of Ethiopia (1960) [11][12].

steps.title: Apply for invalidity, employment-injury, and sector pension benefits
steps.html:
• Identify the applicable statutory pension fund early so medical-board evaluations and contribution histories can be assembled without delay.
  • Public sector employees and civil servants fall under the Public Servants Social Security Administration (PSSSA), governed by Public Servants' Pension Proclamation No. 1267/2022, which covers retirement, invalidity, and work-injury pensions [6][7].
  • Salaried Ethiopian nationals working 45 days or more in private organizations fall under the Private Organization Employees' Social Security Administration (POESSA) pursuant to Private Organization Employees' Pension Proclamation No. 1268/2022 and its implementing regulation [5][16].
  • Review paid sick leave, workplace medical incapacity assessments, and injury compensation protections under Ethiopia's Labour Proclamation No. 1156/2019 [13].

steps.title: Prepare statutory wills and complete non-Apostille consular authentication
steps.html:
• Prepare a formal public, holograph, or legally witnessed oral will satisfying the strict form and capacity rules of Book II, Title V (Successions, Articles 826 and following) of the Civil Code of Ethiopia (1960), keeping in mind how pension rights interact separately from general succession assets under statutory provisions [12].
  • Confirm cross-border authentication steps early because Ethiopia is not a contracting party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, so foreign apostilles are not valid [15].
  • Documents originating inside Ethiopia for foreign use require DARS certification, authentication by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Ethiopia, and legalization by the receiving country's embassy [3][14]; foreign medical reports or powers of attorney destined for Ethiopia require state/local certification, authentication by the issuing Foreign Ministry (such as the U.S. Department of State Office of Authentications), and legalization through the Ethiopian diplomatic mission and Digital MoFA system [8][9].

contacts.name: Documents Authentication and Registration Service
contacts.note: Federal authority under Proclamation No. 922/2015 responsible for domestic Powers of Attorney (wekilina), wills, and document authentication; portal tech line 888.

contacts.name: Public Servants Social Security Administration
contacts.note: Administers federal and public servant retirement, invalidity, and work-injury pensions under Proclamation No. 1267/2022.

contacts.name: Private Organization Employees' Social Security Administration
contacts.note: Administers private-sector invalidity, illness-pension, and injury claims for eligible employees under Proclamation No. 1268/2022.

contacts.name: Embassy of Ethiopia in Washington, D.C.
contacts.note: Handles overseas Ethiopian Power of Attorney (Digital MoFA) and document legalization after U.S. Department of State authentication (3506 International Dr NW).

contacts.name: Ministry of Justice of Ethiopia
contacts.note: Publishes federal authentication proclamations, Regulation No. 451/2019 fee schedules, and social security statutory texts (Addis Ababa).
